question: Build a patch that plays a 440 Hz sine wave at half amplitude on both channels as soon as it is opened with audio on.
Build a patch that mixes a 300 Hz and a 450 Hz sine wave equally and plays them without clipping as soon as it is opened.
Build a simple FM synthesis patch: a 400 Hz carrier modulated by a 100 Hz sine, playing as soon as it is opened, without clipping.
Build a ring modulator patch that multiplies a 500 Hz sine by an 80 Hz sine and plays the result as soon as it is opened.
Build a patch that plays white noise through a low-pass filter with a 500 Hz cutoff as soon as it is opened.
Build a patch that, when opened, plays one 330 Hz note that fades smoothly to silence over one second.
Build a patch that plays a 110 Hz sawtooth wave with no DC offset and no clipping as soon as it is opened.
Build a patch that, when opened, sweeps a sine oscillator from 200 Hz to 800 Hz over two seconds.
Build a patch where a number box sets the pitch of a sine oscillator as a MIDI note number, so entering 69 plays 440 Hz.
Build a patch that, when opened, counts up from 0 by one every 200 milliseconds and prints each number to the Pd window.
Build a patch that, when opened, plays a short sound burst under 200 ms long, followed by a single echo of it one second later, using a delay line.
Build a patch that plays a 440 Hz sine in the left channel only and a 660 Hz sine in the right channel only, as soon as it is opened.
Build a patch that plays white noise through a band-pass filter centred on 1000 Hz with a Q of 20 as soon as it is opened.
Build a wavetable oscillator patch: fill a table with one cycle of a sine wave when the patch opens and play it at 220 Hz.
Build a patch with a toggle that starts and stops a metronome at 250 ms, with each tick playing a short 1000 Hz blip.
Build a tremolo patch: a 300 Hz sine whose level goes up and down 5 times per second, playing as soon as it is opened without clipping.
